lyrics:
[Intro: drum machine tick alone, dark synth pad swells, guitar howl]

[Verse 1: hushed, vocoder shadow, pad and tick]
I saw you on the bridge that night
You didn't see me see
The water kept its mouth shut tight
But water talks to me

[Chorus: quiet, restrained, electric piano chords join]
Something's in the wires tonight
Something's leaning on the door
I've carried this since I was young
Wait for the thunder
It's coming for sure

[Verse 2: hushed, distant guitar swell]
You shook my hand, you wore the grin
You asked about my year
I've got a drawer I keep it in
The thing you did, right here

[Chorus: quiet, slightly more intense, low synth note]
Something's in the wires tonight
Something's leaning on the door
I've carried this since I was young
Wait for the thunder
It's coming for sure

[Verse 3: nearly whispered, most exposed]
Don't hand me that Sunday voice
I heard it break in two
The kindest thing I've ever done
Is not say what I knew

[Break: all instruments stop, whispered, silence]
Wait
Wait

[Drum Fill: huge descending tom fill, gated reverb, crash]

[Chorus: full band, pounding live drums, raw shouted vocal]
Something's in the wires tonight!
Something's leaning on the door!
I've carried this since I was young
Here comes the thunder
I'm not carrying it anymore

[Chorus: full band, ad-libbed echoes]
Something's in the wires tonight!
Something's leaning on the door!
I've carried this since I was young
Here comes the thunder
I'm not carrying it anymore

[Outro: drums keep hammering, vocal repeats and fades]
(Wait for the thunder)
You know, you know I know
(Wait for the thunder)
You know, you know I know
(Wait for the thunder)
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 94 BPM, 4/4, E minor, three slow chords that circle without resolving. Dark, still and menacing for most of its length, then explosive.

VOICE: Male tenor, hushed and close, sung almost under his breath with clenched restraint. In the verses the voice is doubled by a faint robotic vocoder layer, making it sound cold and distant. After the drum fill the processing is stripped away and he sings out raw, loud and angry, with echoes repeating his last words.

INSTRUMENTS: A vintage analog drum machine playing a soft, ticking, hypnotic pattern (the pulse). A dark, slowly swelling analog synth pad. Sparse electric piano chords with a tremolo shimmer. Distorted electric guitar that enters only as long, feedback-like swells. A deep, simple bass guitar that arrives with the drums. Then a real drum kit: huge concert toms and a snare with dramatic gated reverb.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, drum-machine tick alone, then the synth pad swelling in and one distant guitar howl. 0:30 Verse 1, voice with vocoder shadow over pad and tick. 0:56 Refrain 1, electric piano chords join. 1:27 Verse 2, a second guitar swell. 1:53 Refrain 2, slightly more intense, a low synth note added. 2:24 Verse 3, the most exposed moment, the voice nearly a whisper. 2:50 Pre-thunder, every instrument cuts out. Two whispered words, then one full bar of total silence. 2:58 The fill: a tumbling, descending run of twelve strokes across four deep toms, soaked in gated reverb, landing on a crash. 3:01 Refrain with full band, live drums pounding, bass in, voice unprocessed and shouting. 3:32 Second full refrain with ad-libbed echoes. 4:03 Outro, drums keep hammering while the vocal repeats and fades, ending at 4:35.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Extremely sparse and dark for three minutes with a wide, empty stereo field, so that the drums sound gigantic when they arrive. Gated room reverb on the kit: enormous, then abruptly cut off.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: 2:58. The silence, then the tom fill. Everything in the arrangement exists to make those two seconds land.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: A sub-bass drop under the bar of silence, felt more than heard, and a faint field recording of approaching thunder beneath verse 3.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Cold control, pressure, rupture, then release.

WHAT IT IS ABOUT

Someone has kept quiet for years about what they saw one night on a bridge. They shake the hand, they return the smile, and they wait. Three minutes in, the sky breaks.

THE OTHER WAYS TO HEAR IT

Hear it as: a betrayal finally confronted; a family secret; a crime witnessed; a reckoning with your own past self (the 'you' can be the singer); or plain dread about a storm, real or political, that everyone can feel coming. The lyric never states what happened, so listeners will invent the story, as they did with the original.

ENGINEERED HOOKS AND THE DESIGNED MISHEARING

Borrowed mechanics: an accusation with no context, long near-silences, and a single delayed instrumental event that the title actually names, so people tell each other to 'wait for the thunder'. The bridge-and-water imagery is planted for legend-making. Designed mishearing: 'Wait for the thunder' is heard as 'Weight of the thunder' and 'Wake for the thunder'.
